newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents per lb higher on Tuesday, as traders expected the market to follow-through on Monday's strong finish.

New York arabica futures rose sharply on Monday, on speculative buying amid forecasts for cold weather in Brazil. July surged 16.05 cents per lb, to 253.30 cents, after ranging between 256.00 and 235.50 cents. September jumped 9.45 cents, to 223.60 cents, while the back months closed up 7.25 to 9.00.
The July/September spread, a barometer of near-term availability, bulged to 29.70 cents today from 23.10 cents on Friday.

Brazil's coffee belt appeared to have seen the worst of a passing polar air mass, with cooperative officials in key regions confirming a slightly milder night and no reports of any frosts on coffee farms.
Weather Services Corp. said on Tuesday that temperatures would be cool this morning in Brazil's coffee belt, but no damaging cold was expected.
Brazil's weather is expected to turn milder over the next couple of days, with low temperatures on Wednesday in the 40s to lower 50s F. Thursday's lows will range from 45 to 55 F, WSC said.
After Monday's close, the CSCE said certified coffee stocks rose by 590 60-kg bags as of June 6, to 44,215 bags, There were 2,578 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders said July would to run into some resistance at 260.00 cents, with stronger resistance seen at 263.00. Support was seen at 245.00, then 238.00-239.00.
London robusta futures were higher in light volume early Monday. LIFFE July rose $70 at the midday break, to $1,960, while September was $67 higher, at $1,992.
